name: Mother's Prayer
slug: An ancient Navi sacred prophecy of catastrophe, a hero, and self-rewriting fate that currently describes Gerk and serves Atlas.
description: Mother's Prayer, also known as the Mother's Prophecy, Mother's Tale, or Mother's Tales, is an ancient sacred prophecy originating in the early history of the Navi in Midgard and across Atlas. It describes a recurring cycle involving catastrophe, a hero, difficult choices, gates and arches, dormant keys, and individuals connected to the Great Eldarin Tree. The prophecy can apparently change itself when a son or daughter of the Tree chooses an independent path, suggesting that it records possibilities rather than dictating fate. It is associated with the mysterious process by which individuals are brought forth when Atlas requires them, and its purpose appears connected to the health and prosperity of Atlas as a whole. The prophecy was unintentionally set in motion when the Navi created the keystones, and Gerk is currently identified as the individual described by it.

log.summary: The **Mother’s Prayer** was clarified as a recurring, self-rewriting prophecy tied to the Navi, the Great Eldarin Tree, and the needs of Atlas. During the session, Gerk was confirmed as the individual currently described by the prophecy, which contains factual information about him and someone close to him without determining his choices. The party learned that the prophecy exists in multiple journals and tomes written by different authors, and that its tales can apparently rewrite themselves when a child of the Tree chooses an independent path. The prophecy’s process seems to bring forth individuals when Atlas needs them and follows a recurring cycle of catastrophe, a hero, and increasingly difficult choices. The creation of the keystones unintentionally initiated the Mother’s Prayer, whose purpose appears to concern the health and prosperity of all Atlas rather than solely the Great Eldarin Tree. The Tree itself has diminished over time, though a new bud is expected at the end of the current growing season.
